claim: The evolution of high acuity vision in fishes was directly associated with their unique pH-sensitive hemoglobins that allow O2 to be delivered to the retina at PO2s more than ten-fold that of arterial blood.
source: Previously, we showed that the evolution of high acuity vision in fishes was directly associated with their unique pH-sensitive hemoglobins that allow O2 to be delivered to the retina at PO2s more than ten-fold that of arterial blood (Damsgaard et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Damsgaard et al., 2019).

claim: Vacuolar-type H+-ATPase and plasma-accessible carbonic anhydrase in the vascular structure supplying the retina act together to acidify the red blood cell leading to O2 secretion.
source: Here, we show strong evidence that vacuolar-type H+-ATPase and plasma-accessible carbonic anhydrase in the vascular structure supplying the retina act together to acidify the red blood cell leading to O2 secretion.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including immunohistochemistry, western blotting, and in vivo pharmacological inhibition experiments.

claim: The oxygen secretion pathway primarily affects the oxygenation of the inner retina involved in signal processing and transduction.
source: In vivo data indicate that this pathway primarily affects the oxygenation of the inner retina involved in signal processing and transduction, and that the evolution of this pathway was tightly associated with the morphological expansion of the inner retina.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo electroretinogram data showing differential effects on inner versus outer retina.

claim: The evolution of the oxygen secretion pathway was tightly associated with the morphological expansion of the inner retina.
source: In vivo data indicate that this pathway primarily affects the oxygenation of the inner retina involved in signal processing and transduction, and that the evolution of this pathway was tightly associated with the morphological expansion of the inner retina.
evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic comparative analysis of retinal morphology across species with and without choroid rete mirabile.

claim: The mechanism for retinal oxygenation played a vital role in the adaptive evolution of vision in teleost fishes.
source: We conclude that this mechanism for retinal oxygenation played a vital role in the adaptive evolution of vision in teleost fishes.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the functional and evolutionary data presented in the study.

claim: The retina of vertebrates has a very high metabolic rate that must be supported by an adequate supply of O2.
source: The retina of vertebrates, containing the light-sensitive photoreceptors required for visual perception, has a very high metabolic rate that must be supported by an adequate supply of O2 (Linsenmeier and Braun, 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Pigmented RBCs in capillaries on the vitreous side of the retina scatter incoming light and absorb photons before they reach the photoreceptors.
source: However, pigmented RBCs in capillaries on the vitreous side of the retina scatter incoming light and absorb photons before they reach the photoreceptors (Buttery et al., 1991; Chase, 1982; Country, 2017; Damsgaard et al., 2019; Yu and Cringle, 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to established literature.

claim: Only the choroidal vessels lining the back of the retina perfuse the retinae of most vertebrates.
source: The result may be an impairment of visual acuity, which may explain why only the choroidal vessels lining the back of the retina (also called the choriocapillaris) perfuse the retinae of most vertebrates (Country, 2017) (see Figure 1 for retinal anatomy).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: There is a tradeoff between retinal O2 supply and visual performance common to all vertebrates.
source: The combination of a high O2 demand and limited O2 diffusion associated with this anatomical arrangement introduces a tradeoff between retinal O2 supply and visual performance common to all vertebrates (Damsgaard et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and represents an inference from anatomical and physiological constraints.

claim: Some teleost fishes evolved a unique solution to ensure sufficient O2 delivery to their thick retina by using an exceptional system for O2 supply, which delivers O2 at a PO2 far above that of the arterial blood.
source: In stark contrast, some teleost fishes evolved a unique solution to ensure sufficient O2 delivery to their thick retina despite a complete lack of internal capillaries by using an exceptional system for O2 supply, which delivers O2 at a PO2 far above that of the arterial blood (henceforth: O2 secretion).
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about teleost fish retinal physiology.

claim: A similar O2 secretion mechanism was initially described in the teleost swim bladder, where blood acidification in the capillaries drives O2 from hemoglobin into the swim bladder lumen.
source: A similar O2 secretion mechanism was initially described in the teleost swim bladder, where blood acidification in the capillaries drives O2 from hemoglobin (Hb) into the swim bladder lumen in order to regulate buoyancy against high hydrostatic pressures at depth (Berenbrink et al., 2005; Steen, 1963a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Blood PO2 can increase from around 85 mmHg in the central arteries to beyond 1300 mmHg in the retina of some fish species.
source: Later, O2 secretion was also described in the teleost retina, where blood PO2 can increase from around 85 mmHg in the central arteries to beyond 1300 mmHg in the retina of some fish species (Randall and Cameron, 1973; Wittenberg and Wittenberg, 1962).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Oxygenated blood is supplied to the retina from the pseudobranch that drains into a counter-current rete, the choroid rete mirabile.
source: Oxygenated blood is supplied to the retina from the pseudobranch that drains into a counter-current rete (Barnett, 1951; Copeland, 1980; Müller, 1841; Walls, 1942), the choroid rete mirabile, which allows the high PO2 to be magnified and localized behind the retina by permitting diffusion of O2 from the venous to the arterial side of the rete.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The evolutionary innovation of the choroid rete provided a high O2 flux to the thick fish retina without obstructing the optical path.
source: The evolutionary innovation of the choroid rete provided a high O2 flux to the thick fish retina without obstructing the optical path.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the anatomical and functional properties of the choroid rete.

claim: The choroid rete likely enabled an increase in visual performance that may have facilitated niche expansions and novel feeding types and may have contributed to the explosive adaptive radiation of the teleosts.
source: It likely enabled an increase in visual performance that may have facilitated niche expansions and novel feeding types and may have contributed to the explosive adaptive radiation of the teleosts, that today, represent half of all vertebrates (Berenbrink et al., 2005; Randall et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is speculative and based on inference from the functional advantages of the choroid rete, supported by citations.

claim: Rainbow trout has a higher retinal PO2 compared to white sturgeon.
source: Partial pressure of O2 (PO2) distribution in the retina of rainbow trout (red) and white sturgeon (blue) (C) showing that rainbow trout has a higher PO2 (linear mixed-effects model, n = 6 [3 for each species], β ± SE = 390±75.8 mmHg, t = 5.14, p<0.001)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements and statistical analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Rainbow trout has a steeper PO2 gradient compared to white sturgeon.
source: and a steeper PO2 gradient (linear mixed-effects model, n = 6 [3 for each species], β ± SE = −1.06 ± 0.0859 mmHg µm−1, t = −12.4, p<0.001) when compared to white sturgeon.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements and statistical analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Rainbow trout possesses a choroid rete mirabile.
source: Histology indicates a thick retina and presence of a choroid rete mirabile in the rainbow trout and a thin retina and absence of a choroid rete mirabile in the white sturgeon.
evidence: This claim is supported by histological evidence shown in Figure 1A.

claim: White sturgeon lacks a choroid rete mirabile.
source: Histology indicates a thick retina and presence of a choroid rete mirabile in the rainbow trout and a thin retina and absence of a choroid rete mirabile in the white sturgeon.
evidence: This claim is supported by histological evidence shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The hallmark of retinal O2 secretion is the Root effect of teleost Hbs, where H+-binding to Hb reduces not only its O2 affinity but also its O2 carrying capacity.
source: The hallmark of retinal O2 secretion is the Root effect of teleost Hbs, where H+-binding to Hb reduces not only its O2 affinity but also its O2 carrying capacity (Pelster and Weber, 1991; Root, 1931; Waser and Heisler, 2005; Weber and Fago, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature on the Root effect.

claim: Reductions in RBC pH lead to a significant right-shift of the O2 equilibrium curve and a pronounced increase in blood PO2.
source: Thus, reductions in RBC pH lead to a significant right-shift of the O2 equilibrium curve and, consequently, a pronounced increase in blood PO2.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of hemoglobin oxygen binding properties.

claim: The pseudobranch slightly acidifies the blood before it reaches the eye, but this acidification is not sufficient to activate the Root effect.
source: While the pseudobranch slightly acidifies the blood before it reaches the eye, this acidification is not sufficient to activate the Root effect (Bridges et al., 1998; Kern et al., 2002; Waser and Heisler, 2005; Waser and Heisler, 2004), as otherwise, this would lead to a maladaptive loss of O2 to the surrounding water.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: An additional source of H+-secretion of the blood draining the pseudobranch is required to activate the Root effect and induce retinal O2 secretion.
source: Thus, an additional source of H+-secretion of the blood draining the pseudobranch is required to activate the Root effect and induce retinal O2 secretion.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the insufficient acidification by the pseudobranch alone.

claim: Vacuolar-type H+-ATPase (VHA) is a key candidate for excreting H+s from the endothelial cells into the lumen.
source: We propose that a key candidate for excreting H+s from the endothelial cells into the lumen is the vacuolar-type H+-ATPase (VHA).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on the known function of VHA.

claim: VHA uses the energy from ATP hydrolysis to transport H+ across biological membranes.
source: This multi-subunit enzyme uses the energy from ATP hydrolysis to transport H+ across biological membranes (Tresguerres, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature on VHA function.

claim: VHA is expressed in cells within the pseudobranch and the swimbladder gas-gland.
source: VHA is expressed in cells within the pseudobranch and the swimbladder gas-gland (Boesch et al., 2003; Kern et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: H+s do not rapidly cross the red blood cell membrane and must be combined with HCO3− to form CO2 that readily diffuses across the RBC membrane.
source: However, H+s do not rapidly cross the red blood cell membrane and must be combined with HCO3− to form CO2 (HCO3− dehydration) that readily diffuses across the RBC membrane (Brauner et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature on membrane permeability.

claim: The HCO3− dehydration reaction is slow relative to rates of blood capillary transit.
source: This dehydration reaction is slow relative to rates of blood capillary transit, so we also propose that a catalytic plasma-accessible carbonic anhydrase (paCA) is required to take advantage of VHA H+-excretion for RBC acidification.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of reaction kinetics and is used to support the hypothesis about paCA.

claim: A catalytic plasma-accessible carbonic anhydrase (paCA) is required to take advantage of VHA H+-excretion for RBC acidification.
source: This dehydration reaction is slow relative to rates of blood capillary transit, so we also propose that a catalytic plasma-accessible carbonic anhydrase (paCA) is required to take advantage of VHA H+-excretion for RBC acidification.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: Once CO2 is within the RBC, it must rapidly be converted into H+ by a RBC CA to activate the Root effect.
source: Once CO2 is within the RBC, it must rapidly be converted into H+ by a RBC CA to activate the Root effect, as the vast majority of teleost Hbs are insensitive to direct CO2-binding and respond solely to changes in RBC pH (Damsgaard et al., 2014; Weber and Fago, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature on teleost hemoglobin properties.

claim: The vast majority of teleost Hbs are insensitive to direct CO2-binding and respond solely to changes in RBC pH.
source: Once CO2 is within the RBC, it must rapidly be converted into H+ by a RBC CA to activate the Root effect, as the vast majority of teleost Hbs are insensitive to direct CO2-binding and respond solely to changes in RBC pH (Damsgaard et al., 2014; Weber and Fago, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: VHA and CA4 proteins are present in tissue homogenates of the choroid rete mirabile.
source: Western blotting showed the presence of VHA and CA4 proteins in tissue homogenates of the choroid rete mirabile (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: CA4 and VHA are both present in endothelial cells of the choroid rete mirabile vasculature.
source: To localize these proteins within the choroid rete mirabile, we used immunohistochemistry and confocal super-resolution microscopy on tissue sections, showing that CA4 and VHA were both present in endothelial cells of the choroid rete mirabile vasculature (Figures 2 and 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Both CA4 and VHA are present on the luminal side of the cell nucleus in endothelial cells.
source: Super-resolution images showed that both CA4 and VHA were present on the luminal side of the cell nucleus, likely in association with the plasma membrane of these endothelial cells (Figures 2D and 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figures 2D and 3D.

claim: CA4 and VHA have a plasma-accessible orientation and line the entire vasculature of the choroid rete mirabile in rainbow trout.
source: This finding is consistent with a plasma-accessible orientation of VHA and CA4, and these enzymes seem to line the entire vasculature of the choroid rete mirabile in rainbow trout.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the immunohistochemistry data.

claim: VHA has a robust enzymatic activity in choroid rete mirabile homogenates of 2.20 ± 0.252 µmol ADP h−1 mg protein−1.
source: Lastly, we showed a robust enzymatic activity of VHA in choroid rete mirabile homogenates of 2.20 ± 0.252 µmol ADP h−1 mg protein−1.
evidence: This claim is supported by enzymatic activity assay data.

claim: Under control conditions, choroidal PO2 was 517 ± 95.3 mmHg in rainbow trout.
source: Under control conditions, choroidal PO2 was 517 ± 95.3 mmHg (mean ± standard error of mean, n = 6), which is significantly higher than the typical PO2 values of 85 mmHg in the dorsal aortic blood of rainbow trout (Randall and Cameron, 1973).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo measurements.

claim: Control choroidal PO2 is significantly higher than the typical PO2 values of 85 mmHg in the dorsal aortic blood of rainbow trout.
source: Under control conditions, choroidal PO2 was 517 ± 95.3 mmHg (mean ± standard error of mean, n = 6), which is significantly higher than the typical PO2 values of 85 mmHg in the dorsal aortic blood of rainbow trout (Randall and Cameron, 1973).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of measured data with cited literature values.

claim: Control injection of saline did not affect choroidal PO2.
source: The control injection of saline did not affect choroidal PO2 (linear mixed-effect model followed by Tukey posthoc analysis, n = 6, β ± SE = −32.2 ± 84.7 mmHg, z = −0.380, Holm-adjusted p=0.70, Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: Injection of C18 decreased choroidal PO2 to 226 ± 99.5 mmHg.
source: The subsequent injection of C18 decreased choroidal PO2, to 226 ± 99.5 mmHg (n = 6, β ± SE = −259 ± 84.7 mmHg, z = −3.05, Holm-adjusted p=0.0068, Figure 4), verifying a role of paCA in facilitating Hb-O2 unloading to the retina.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: The C18 injection verifies a role of paCA in facilitating Hb-O2 unloading to the retina.
source: The subsequent injection of C18 decreased choroidal PO2, to 226 ± 99.5 mmHg (n = 6, β ± SE = −259 ± 84.7 mmHg, z = −3.05, Holm-adjusted p=0.0068, Figure 4), verifying a role of paCA in facilitating Hb-O2 unloading to the retina.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental results showing that inhibiting paCA reduces choroidal PO2.

claim: Addition of acetazolamide further decreased choroidal PO2 to 18.3 ± 13.2 mmHg.
source: The addition of acetazolamide further decreased choroidal PO2, to 18.3 ± 13.2 mmHg (n = 6, β ± SE = −207 ± 84.7 mmHg, z = −2.45, Holm-adjusted p=0.0283, Figure 4), indicating an additional involvement of intracellular CAs in acidifying the red blood cell to enhance O2 secretion to the retina.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: Acetazolamide results indicate an additional involvement of intracellular CAs in acidifying the red blood cell to enhance O2 secretion to the retina.
source: The addition of acetazolamide further decreased choroidal PO2, to 18.3 ± 13.2 mmHg (n = 6, β ± SE = −207 ± 84.7 mmHg, z = −2.45, Holm-adjusted p=0.0283, Figure 4), indicating an additional involvement of intracellular CAs in acidifying the red blood cell to enhance O2 secretion to the retina.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental results showing that inhibiting both extra- and intracellular CA further reduces choroidal PO2.

claim: The immunohistochemical and biochemical data strongly support the hypothesis that VHA and paCA act together to facilitate O2 secretion in the teleost retina.
source: These results in combination with the immunohistochemical and biochemical data strongly support the hypothesis that VHA and paCA act together to facilitate O2 secretion in the teleost retina.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: Rainbow trout exhibited the normal features of a vertebrate electroretinogram with distinct a- and b-waves under control conditions.
source: Under control conditions, rainbow trout exhibited the normal features of a vertebrate electroretinogram with distinct a- and b-waves (Figure 5A), representing the hyperpolarization of the photoreceptors and the depolarization of the ON-center bipolar cells within the inner retina, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by electroretinogram data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The a-wave represents the hyperpolarization of the photoreceptors.
source: Under control conditions, rainbow trout exhibited the normal features of a vertebrate electroretinogram with distinct a- and b-waves (Figure 5A), representing the hyperpolarization of the photoreceptors and the depolarization of the ON-center bipolar cells within the inner retina, respectively.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of electroretinogram interpretation.

claim: The b-wave represents the depolarization of the ON-center bipolar cells within the inner retina.
source: Under control conditions, rainbow trout exhibited the normal features of a vertebrate electroretinogram with distinct a- and b-waves (Figure 5A), representing the hyperpolarization of the photoreceptors and the depolarization of the ON-center bipolar cells within the inner retina, respectively.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of electroretinogram interpretation.

claim: The amplitudes of the a- and b-waves of the electroretinogram displayed absolute reductions with reduced choroidal PO2.
source: The amplitudes of the a- and b-waves of the electroretinogram (Va and Vb, respectively) displayed absolute reductions with reduced choroidal PO2 (linear mixed-effect model using log10-transformed PO2, n = 4, β ± SE = 0.383±0.0565, t = 6.79, p<0.001), but with a 2.1-fold greater effect on the b-wave compared to the a-wave (p<0.001).
evidence: This claim is supported by electroretinogram data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: The b-wave showed a 2.1-fold greater effect from reduced choroidal PO2 compared to the a-wave.
source: The amplitudes of the a- and b-waves of the electroretinogram (Va and Vb, respectively) displayed absolute reductions with reduced choroidal PO2 (linear mixed-effect model using log10-transformed PO2, n = 4, β ± SE = 0.383±0.0565, t = 6.79, p<0.001), but with a 2.1-fold greater effect on the b-wave compared to the a-wave (p<0.001).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of electroretinogram data.

claim: The inner retina is more sensitive to changes in choroidal PO2 compared to the outer retina.
source: This finding supports the second hypothesis that the inner retina is more sensitive to changes in choroidal PO2 compared to the outer retina.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the differential effects on a-wave and b-wave amplitudes.

claim: ITa was impaired by reductions in choroidal PO2.
source: The data showed that ITa was impaired by reductions in choroidal PO2 (linear mixed-effect model using log10-transformed PO2 in mmHg, n = 4, β ± SE = −53.2 ± 7.93, t = −6.70, p<0.001).
evidence: This claim is supported by electroretinogram data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: ITb was similarly affected by reductions in choroidal PO2.
source: ITb was similarly affected by reductions in choroidal PO2 (linear mixed-effect model using log10-transformed PO2, n = 4, β ± SE = −52.8 ± 11.8, t = −4.47, p<0.001).
evidence: This claim is supported by electroretinogram data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Species with a choroid rete mirabile have significantly thicker inner retina (204 ± 92.6 µm) compared to species without (97.1 ± 37.0 µm).
source: This analysis showed significantly thicker inner retina in species with a choroid rete mirabile (204 ± 92.6 µm [mean ± s.d.], n = 19) compared to species without (97.1 ± 37.0 µm [mean ± s.d.], n = 12) (phylogenetic analysis of variance simulation, p<0.001, n = 31).
evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic comparative analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: There are no differences in the thickness of the outer retina between species with and without a choroid rete mirabile.
source: In contrast, the analysis did not show any differences in the thickness of the outer retina between species with and without a choroid rete mirabile (phylogenetic analysis of variance simulation, p=0.51, n = 31).
evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic comparative analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Significant differences in retinal layer thickness between species with and without a choroid rete mirabile were identified in the four layers positioned most distant to the choroid.
source: Specifically, we identified significant differences in retinal layer thickness between species with and without a choroid rete mirabile in the four layers positioned most distant to the choroid (i.e. the inner nuclear layer (p=0.0499, n = 31), the inner plexiform layer (p=0.00754, n = 31), the ganglion cell layer (p=0.104, n = 31), and the nerve fiber layer (p=0.00726, n = 31); Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic comparative analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The evolutionary gains and losses of the choroid rete mirabile during teleost radiation had large effects on the morphology of the inner retina, but not the outer retina.
source: These findings support the third hypothesis that the evolutionary gains and losses of the choroid rete mirabile during teleost radiation had large effects on the morphology of the inner retina, but not the outer retina.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the phylogenetic comparative analysis.

claim: The 10-fold higher choroidal PO2 associated with the presence of a choroid rete mirabile was not associated with a proportional difference in retinal thickness between trout and sturgeon.
source: However, the 10-fold higher choroidal PO2 associated with the presence of a choroid rete mirabile was not associated with a proportional difference in retinal thickness between trout and sturgeon.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of data from the two species.

claim: The slope of the PO2 profile was 6.2-fold higher in trout compared to sturgeon, which equals a proportionally higher O2 consumption rate in the trout retina than the sturgeon retina.
source: Instead, the slope of the PO2 profile was 6.2-fold higher in trout compared to sturgeon, which equals a proportionally higher O2 consumption rate in the trout retina than the sturgeon retina (assuming equal diffusive capacity for O2 in the retinae of the two species).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the measured PO2 profiles, with an assumption about diffusive capacity.

claim: The origin of O2 secretion permitted not only the evolution of a thicker retina, but also the evolution of much higher metabolic rates of the retina.
source: Despite depending on two species only, this data set strongly suggests that the origin of O2 secretion permitted not only the evolution of a thicker retina, but also the evolution of much higher metabolic rates of the retina.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the comparison of trout and sturgeon data.

claim: Increased retinal thickness is typically associated with a higher area density of photoreceptors.
source: Increased retinal thickness is typically associated with a higher area density of photoreceptors (Jeffery and Williams, 1994; Potier et al., 2017; Querubin et al., 2009), which may explain the higher O2 consumption rate, and which may provide an additional advantage to vision in terms on increased spatial resolution (Damsgaard et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Higher photoreceptor density may explain the higher O2 consumption rate and may provide an additional advantage to vision in terms of increased spatial resolution.
source: Increased retinal thickness is typically associated with a higher area density of photoreceptors (Jeffery and Williams, 1994; Potier et al., 2017; Querubin et al., 2009), which may explain the higher O2 consumption rate, and which may provide an additional advantage to vision in terms on increased spatial resolution (Damsgaard et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is speculative and based on inference from cited literature.

claim: The choroid rete mirabile allows for the generation of exceptionally high PO2s in the retina.
source: The choroid rete mirabile in the eye of teleost fishes allows for the generation of exceptionally high PO2s in the retina and permitted the functional evolution of some of the most extreme retinal phenotypes among vertebrates with substantial expansions in the retinal layers associated with visual processing.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data presented in the study.

claim: The choroid rete mirabile permitted the functional evolution of some of the most extreme retinal phenotypes among vertebrates with substantial expansions in the retinal layers associated with visual processing.
source: The choroid rete mirabile in the eye of teleost fishes allows for the generation of exceptionally high PO2s in the retina and permitted the functional evolution of some of the most extreme retinal phenotypes among vertebrates with substantial expansions in the retinal layers associated with visual processing.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the functional and evolutionary data presented.

claim: The VHA-paCA pathway for blood acidification represents a novel physiological function of the choroid rete mirabile in addition to counter-current gas-exchange.
source: Our identification of the VHA-paCA pathway for blood acidification to facilitate retinal O2 secretion represents a novel physiological function of the choroid rete mirabile in addition to counter-current gas-exchange, which together permit greatly enhanced O2 delivery to the retina.
evidence: This claim is based on the novel findings presented in the study.

claim: The origin of O2 secretion not only permitted the evolution of a thicker retina, but also added fuel to the metabolic fire to visual perception.
source: Our data further suggest that the origin of O2 secretion not only permitted the evolution of a thicker retina, but also added fuel to the metabolic fire to visual perception.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the data showing higher metabolic rates in species with O2 secretion.

claim: The advantages to vision from O2 secretion possibly allowed teleost fishes to explore new food resources and colonize novel environments.
source: These significant advantages to vision possibly allowed teleost fishes to explore new food resources and colonize novel environments, which may have contributed to the extraordinary adaptive radiation of the teleost fishes, which today represent half of all vertebrates (Berenbrink et al., 2005; Randall et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is speculative and based on inference from the functional advantages demonstrated, supported by citations.

claim: The advantages to vision from O2 secretion may have contributed to the extraordinary adaptive radiation of the teleost fishes.
source: These significant advantages to vision possibly allowed teleost fishes to explore new food resources and colonize novel environments, which may have contributed to the extraordinary adaptive radiation of the teleost fishes, which today represent half of all vertebrates (Berenbrink et al., 2005; Randall et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is speculative and based on inference from the functional advantages demonstrated, supported by citations.

claim: Teleost fishes today represent half of all vertebrates.
source: These significant advantages to vision possibly allowed teleost fishes to explore new food resources and colonize novel environments, which may have contributed to the extraordinary adaptive radiation of the teleost fishes, which today represent half of all vertebrates (Berenbrink et al., 2005; Randall et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Maximal transverse thickness of the retina was 135 µm in sturgeon and 425 µm in trout.
source: Maximal transverse thickness of the retina was 135 and 425 µm in sturgeon and trout, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by histological measurements.

claim: PO2 in the choroid was 732 ± 58.6 mmHg in rainbow trout and 71.22 ± 4.94 mmHg in white sturgeon.
source: As predicted, we found a much higher PO2 in the retina of rainbow trout compared to that of white sturgeon (linear mixed-effect model, n = 6 [3 for each species], β ± SE = 390±75.8 mmHg, t = 5.14, p<0.001) with a PO2 of 732 ± 58.6 and 71.22 ± 4.94 mmHg in the choroid of rainbow trout and white sturgeon, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by direct measurements using PO2 electrodes.

claim: VHA is predicted to pump H+s into the lumen of the choroid rete mirabile.
source: Here, VHA is predicted to pump H+s into the lumen of the choroid rete mirabile, where paCA catalyzes the dehydration of H+ and HCO3- into CO2 for RBC acidification.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the localization and functional data presented.

claim: paCA catalyzes the dehydration of H+ and HCO3- into CO2 for RBC acidification in the choroid rete mirabile.
source: Here, VHA is predicted to pump H+s into the lumen of the choroid rete mirabile, where paCA catalyzes the dehydration of H+ and HCO3- into CO2 for RBC acidification.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the localization and functional data presented.

claim: Inhibiting paCA with C18 resulted in a 60% reduction in choroidal PO2.
source: This pathway is very significant for O2 secretion, as inhibition of paCA with C18 resulted in a 60% reduction in choroidal PO2.
evidence: This claim is based on calculation from the experimental data showing reduction from ~517 to ~226 mmHg.

claim: Blood supplied from the pseudobranch is actively acidified within the choroid rete mirabile to activate the Root effect before the blood reaches the retina.
source: Thus, our data suggest that blood supplied from the pseudobranch is actively acidified within the choroid rete mirabile to activate the Root effect before the blood reaches the retina.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: The pseudobranch and choroid rete mirabile may act in concert to actively augment O2 unloading from Hb within the rete.
source: This pathway does not contradict pseudobranchial H+-secretion, as proposed earlier, but instead indicates that the two tissues may act in concert to actively augment O2 unloading from Hb within the rete.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the data and integration with previous knowledge.

claim: Choroidal PO2 remained above typical arterial values after paCA inhibition by C18.
source: Furthermore, our in vivo data suggest that the VHA – paCA pathway may not be the only mechanism for blood acidification to drive retinal O2 secretion, as choroidal PO2 remained above typical arterial values after paCA inhibition by C18.
evidence: This claim is based on the experimental observation that PO2 was ~226 mmHg after C18, which is above the typical arterial value of 85 mmHg.

claim: Pathways for anaerobic CO2 production may contribute to retinal O2 secretion.
source: These results are indicative of pathways for anaerobic CO2 production contributing to retinal O2 secretion, where the produced CO2 diffuses via the plasma and directly into the RBC without the need for paCA.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the observation that O2 secretion persists after paCA inhibition.

claim: The pentose phosphate shunt may be involved in blood acidification in the retina.
source: Such pathways may include the pentose phosphate shunt, which has been suggested earlier to be involved in blood acidification in the retina (Bridges et al., 1998; Pelster and Weber, 1991).
evidence: This claim is speculative and supported by citations to previous suggestions in the literature.

claim: Reduced amplitudes and increased implicit times of the a- and b-waves in the electroretinogram occur upon reductions in choroidal PO2.
source: Our data showed a strong relationship between choroidal PO2 and retinal function with reduced amplitudes and increased implicit times of the a- and b-waves in the electroretinogram upon reductions in choroidal PO2.
evidence: This claim is supported by the electroretinogram data presented.

claim: Earlier studies showed pronounced changes in the features of the electroretinogram upon acetazolamide administration.
source: Earlier studies showed pronounced changes in the features of the electroretinogram upon acetazolamide administration (Fonner et al., 1973).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Acetazolamide administration had been observed to reduce retinal PO2 in separate studies.
source: These changes were linked to retinal hypoxemia, as acetazolamide administration had been observed to reduce retinal PO2 in separate studies (Fairbanks et al., 1969; Fairbanks et al., 1974).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The a-wave amplitude appears relatively unaffected by progressive retinal hypoxemia at high choroidal PO2, but rapidly decreases with reductions in choroidal PO2 below ~100 mmHg.
source: Our data showed that the a-wave amplitude appears relatively unaffected by progressive retinal hypoxemia at high choroidal PO2, but rapidly decreases with reductions in choroidal PO2 below ~100 mmHg.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of the electroretinogram data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Photoreceptor function was only affected by retinal hypoxemia when choroidal PO2 fell below normal arterial levels.
source: These data indicate that photoreceptor function was only affected by retinal hypoxemia when choroidal PO2 fell below normal arterial levels.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the a-wave amplitude data.

claim: The b-wave amplitude showed higher sensitivity to a reduction in choroidal PO2.
source: In contrast, the b-wave amplitude showed higher sensitivity to a reduction in choroidal PO2, suggesting a more pronounced dependence of the inner retinal layers to the mechanism of O2 secretion by the choroid rete.
evidence: This claim is supported by the electroretinogram data.

claim: Inner retinal layers have a more pronounced dependence on the mechanism of O2 secretion by the choroid rete.
source: In contrast, the b-wave amplitude showed higher sensitivity to a reduction in choroidal PO2, suggesting a more pronounced dependence of the inner retinal layers to the mechanism of O2 secretion by the choroid rete.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the differential sensitivity of the b-wave.

claim: Retinal hypoxemia likely impairs the rate of oxidative phosphorylation in the mitochondria followed by the inability to maintain the transmembrane ionic gradients required for phototransduction.
source: These results show a tremendous sensitivity of the retina to reductions in choroidal PO2 where retinal hypoxemia likely impairs the rate of oxidative phosphorylation in the mitochondria followed by the inability to maintain the transmembrane ionic gradients required for phototransduction (Bickler and Buck, 2007; Boutilier and St-Pierre, 2000).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the functional data and supported by citations to established mechanisms.

claim: The photoreceptors comprising the outer retina lie directly adjacent to the choroid and experience the highest part of the O2 diffusion gradient.
source: These differences in sensitivity of the inner and outer retina to reductions in choroidal PO2 possibly stems from their different positions relative to the O2 supply from the choroid rete: The photoreceptors comprising the outer retina lie directly adjacent to the choroid and experience the highest part of the O2 diffusion gradient and are therefore less sensitive to reductions in choroidal PO2.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from anatomical position and the measured PO2 gradients.

claim: The synaptic layers comprising the inner retina are positioned further from the choroid and are therefore much more affected by reductions in choroidal PO2.
source: However, the synaptic layers comprising the inner retina are positioned further from the choroid and are, therefore, much more affected by reductions in choroidal PO2.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from anatomical position and the functional data.

claim: Any phenotypic changes in the capacity to deliver O2 at a high PO2 in the retina have the most pronounced effects on the function of the inner retina.
source: These results suggest that any phenotypic changes in the capacity to deliver O2 at a high PO2 in the retina have the most pronounced effects on the function of the inner retina.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the differential sensitivity data.

claim: Any evolutionary change that increases choroidal PO2 may act to offset an O2 diffusion limitation on inner retinal O2 supply and be a pre-requisite for the evolutionary expansion of the inner retina.
source: Our in vivo identification of a higher PO2 sensitivity of the inner- versus the outer retina suggests that any evolutionary change that increases choroidal PO2 may act to offset an O2 diffusion limitation on inner retinal O2 supply and, thus, be a pre-requisite for the evolutionary expansion of the inner retina.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the functional sensitivity data.

claim: The O2 diffusion limitation to retinal thickness is mainly attributed to an O2 constraint on the inner retinal morphology.
source: Taken together, our in vivo and phylogenetic data independently suggests that the O2 diffusion limitation to retinal thickness proposed in several studies (Buttery et al., 1991; Chase, 1982; Country, 2017; Damsgaard et al., 2019; Yu and Cringle, 2001) is mainly attributed to an O2 constraint on the inner retinal morphology.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from both the functional and phylogenetic data, supported by citations.

claim: A thicker inner retina can house more synaptic connections for intra-retinal detection of motion, changes in brightness, and contrast generation in the inner plexiform layer.
source: A thicker inner retina can house more synaptic connections for intra-retinal detection of motion, changes in brightness, and contrast generation in the inner plexiform layer before visual information is relayed via the ganglion cells to the brain (Rodieck, 1998).
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of retinal anatomy and function, supported by a citation.

claim: The origin of retinal O2 secretion around 270 million years ago in a common teleost ancestor was associated with improved visual processing.
source: Thus, our findings imply that the origin of retinal O2 secretion around 270 million years ago in a common teleost ancestor was associated with improved visual processing, which may have facilitated novel feeding strategies involving visual prey identification and tracking.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the functional and evolutionary data.

claim: Improved visual processing from O2 secretion may have facilitated novel feeding strategies involving visual prey identification and tracking.
source: Thus, our findings imply that the origin of retinal O2 secretion around 270 million years ago in a common teleost ancestor was associated with improved visual processing, which may have facilitated novel feeding strategies involving visual prey identification and tracking.
evidence: This claim is speculative and based on inference from the functional advantages.

claim: Multiple groups have secondarily lost the O2 secretory mechanism.
source: Further, multiple groups have secondarily lost the O2 secretory mechanism (Berenbrink et al., 2005; Damsgaard et al., 2019), which correspondingly suggest, that these groups have reduced capacities for visual processing.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Groups that have lost the O2 secretory mechanism have reduced capacities for visual processing.
source: Further, multiple groups have secondarily lost the O2 secretory mechanism (Berenbrink et al., 2005; Damsgaard et al., 2019), which correspondingly suggest, that these groups have reduced capacities for visual processing.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the loss of the mechanism and its functional consequences.

claim: C18 is a functionally membrane-impermeable CA inhibitor within the duration of the experiment.
source: Therefore, we instrumented anesthetized rainbow trout with electrodes in the retina for measuring an electroretinogram and an ultra-thin PO2-electrode in the choroid of the counter lateral eye to measure choroidal PO2. A dorsal aortic catheter was used to deliver arterial injections of saline (control), C18 (a functionally membrane-impermeable CA inhibitor within the duration of the experiment), and acetazolamide (a much more membrane-permeable CA inhibitor that affects both extracellular and intracellular CA) (see Figure 4—figure supplement 1 for experimental setup and timeline) (Rummer et al., 2013; Scozzafava et al., 2000; Supuran, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature on C18 properties.

claim: Acetazolamide is a much more membrane-permeable CA inhibitor that affects both extracellular and intracellular CA.
source: Therefore, we instrumented anesthetized rainbow trout with electrodes in the retina for measuring an electroretinogram and an ultra-thin PO2-electrode in the choroid of the counter lateral eye to measure choroidal PO2. A dorsal aortic catheter was used to deliver arterial injections of saline (control), C18 (a functionally membrane-impermeable CA inhibitor within the duration of the experiment), and acetazolamide (a much more membrane-permeable CA inhibitor that affects both extracellular and intracellular CA) (see Figure 4—figure supplement 1 for experimental setup and timeline) (Rummer et al., 2013; Scozzafava et al., 2000; Supuran, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature on acetazolamide properties.

claim: The only vessel to enter the interior vitreous humor of the eye is the falciform process artery supplying the retractor lentis muscle.
source: The only vessel to enter the interior vitreous humor of the eye is the falciform process artery supplying the retractor lentis muscle.
evidence: This claim is supported by the micro-CT vascular cast data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The falciform process artery is supplied by the lentiform body that receives its blood supply from the lentiform artery.
source: The falciform process artery is supplied by the lentiform body that receives its blood supply from the lentiform artery.
evidence: This claim is supported by the micro-CT vascular cast data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.
